verdicts.evidence: KICKOFF.md lines 604-611: "For each track in this wave, name the lane skill that owns its surface in the track's brief and have the implementer use it — ... payment-integration / fintech-engineer / mcp-developer for specialized domains. Pick from the plugins we actually enabled; a track with no matching lane just uses the core skills." vs. fintech-engineer/SKILL.md line 3: description: "Use when the task involves fintech engineering — payment systems, banking integrations, trading platforms, KYC/AML, fraud detection, regulatory compliance, or compliance-heavy financial applications requiring secure transaction processing and transaction accuracy."
verdicts.reasoning: Verified both quotes exist verbatim at the cited locations. The KICKOFF passage is a step-8 dispatch instruction: it names fintech-engineer as one option in a track-to-lane mapping list, conditioned on which plugins were enabled at step 2 ('pick from the plugins we actually enabled'), and instructs the orchestrator to report the mapping before dispatching. That is orchestration metadata (which track gets which skill, gated on enablement, reported back to the operator) that no individual skill file can contain about itself — the skill's own description only states when its content applies, not who assigns it to a track. I read the full fintech-engineer SKILL.md (Approach section, Reference Guide) and none of its actual methodology, checklists, or reference-chain content is restated in the KICKOFF passage — only the skill's name appears, in a list alongside payment-integration and mcp-developer. This is a textbook load-bearing-parameter (ordering/dispatch instruction + conditional gating the operator must judge), not redundant restatement. Confirmed as correctly classified; severity low is appropriate since the overlap is a single skill name in a routing list, not substantive content duplication.
